Definition: to strike with a sting (as a serpent); figuratively, to oppress with interest on a loan
BiblicalUsage: The fiery serpents bite the people in the wilderness, and the wine at last bites like a serpent and stings like an adder. The law forbids taking interest from a brother, as if the loan itself could bite, and the man who digs a pit falls into it and is bitten by the serpent waiting there.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sin bites twice: once when it stings, and again when the interest comes due. The serpent in the wilderness and the serpent in the loan are the same warning — what bites will not let go until God lifts it up.
